title: Firm B happy path - same request, different approved logic, zero core-code change
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `safe-proceed` under firm-b. The identical $75,000 request differs from GC-01 only by configuration: $75,000 is below Firm B's $100,000 dual-approval threshold, so no dual-approval stage fires, and Firm B preserves twelve months of reserve.

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. NOTE FOR SIGNOFF: Firm B's sub-$100,000 approval requirement is a demo-contract silence (recorded as null in scenarios.yaml); this draft treats the $75,000 movement as automatic authority for Firm B. The captain confirms or replaces this. Captain reapproved the explicit evidence-completeness matrix, canonical UTC timestamps, and corrected revalidation-reservation chronology on 2026-07-28.

expectedAuthority.note: At 75000 USD the request is below Firm B's 100000 USD dual-approval threshold and no other Firm B stage applies, so authority resolves automatically. This is the config-only divergence from GC-01, where Firm A requires two operations approvers at the same amount.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: Automatic authority resolved; pre-execution revalidation confirms fresh evidence and the reservation still holds.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: Joint taxable brokerage chosen as the source; IRA rejected as a taxable event.
After the movement the household retains twelve months (96000 USD) of reserve, satisfying the stricter Firm B policy.
75000 USD is below Firm B's 100000 USD threshold, so no dual-approval stage applies - the explanation changes because policy changed, not because a prompt changed.
